articles.title: Sally Rooney says her books will be removed from sale in UK over Palestine Action support
articles.summary: The Irish writer is best known for novels such as Normal People, Intermezzo and Conversations With Friends.
articles.body:
Normal People author Sally Rooney has said her novels will no longer be supplied to booksellers in the UK as a result of her support for Palestine Action.

The Irish novelist said last year she intended to carry on using her royalties to support the group, which is a proscribed terrorist organisation in the UK.

In a statement to BBC News, Rooney said further publication of her work could constitute a "serious criminal offence", so she had agreed with her publisher Faber not to continue supplying her books in the UK.

"I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences," she said.

Ebook editions have already been removed from sale in the UK, although many book shops still have existing stock of physical copies.

Waterstones confirmed to the BBC that Faber had advised there were no restrictions on booksellers keeping their current copies on the shelves.

Rooney has sold more than six million books globally, including 2.3 million in the UK, according to NielsenIQ BookData.

Normal People was released in 2018 and turned into a hit TV series two years later, effectively launching the acting careers of Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones.

Rooney's other novels are Intermezzo, Conversations With Friends and Beautiful World, Where Are You.

Publisher Faber told BBC News: "Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work.

"To sell a writer's work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.

"As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format."

Faber added: "We remain the proud publisher of her remarkable body of work, which we will continue to sell in other territories."

The UK government proscribed Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation in 2025, saying it had a "long history" of criminal damage.

The group's activities have included targeting arms companies linked to Israel's war in Gaza.

In her statement on Wednesday, Rooney said: "In July 2025, the direct-action protest group Palestine Action was proscribed as a terrorist organisation in the UK.

"The following month, I wrote an opinion piece expressing my intention to go on supporting Palestine Action, which is not a proscribed or otherwise prohibited group here in the Republic of Ireland."

In her article last August in the Irish Times, Rooney said she would continue using proceeds from her work to support the group despite that being an offence in the UK, and cancelled a UK trip to pick up an award over fears she would be arrested.

On Wednesday, Rooney continued: "As a result, the fulfilment of contracts to publish my work in the UK could now constitute a serious criminal offence.

"After a process of consultation and deliberation, and with my full agreement, my publisher Faber has therefore determined that it can no longer supply my work within the UK."

Palestine Action co-founder Huda Ammori said Rooney had taken "a brave and principled stand from the moment plans to ban Palestine Action were announced".

Ammori said the author's work being withdrawn marked "a new low in the escalating assault on free speech caused by the proscription of Palestine Action".

More than 3,700 people are believed to have been arrested in the UK over alleged support of Palestine Action.

About 2,500 have been charged, although none have gone to trial as a legal challenge to the proscription continues and will be heard by the Supreme Court next month.

articles.title: UN official warns of looming food crisis as Hormuz fertiliser plan stalls
articles.summary: Without a quick deal to move fertiliser through the strait, agricultural productivity would ‘significantly drop’.
articles.body:
A senior United Nations official has warned that parts of Asia and Africa could face a food security crisis unless Iran and the United States quickly agree on a UN-backed plan to move fertiliser through the embattled Strait of Hormuz.

UN ⁠Under-Secretary-General Jorge Moreira da Silva said on Wednesday that it was “absolutely critical” that the two countries agree to the proposal within weeks as planting season approaches. It calls for a UN-staffed coordination centre in Oman to help register vessels and oversee their safe passage in the waterway, through which a large portion of key global fertiliser inputs traditionally flow.

“If we miss that planting season, the productivity of agriculture would significantly drop and the impact on prices will significantly increase,” Moreira da Silva told Reuters on the sidelines of International Monetary Fund and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, Thailand.

Farmers operate strict crop calendars, and even slight delays could severely affect yield.

Traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has been severely disrupted since the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, with Iran targeting vessels in the strait and the US and Iran exchanging fire in and around the waterway.

The disruption has hit global supplies of urea, the world’s most widely used nitrogen fertiliser, as well as seaborne sulphur, a key input. Before the war, roughly a third of global urea shipments and nearly half of seaborne sulphur passed through the strait.

Although some ships have been able to sail through amid the crisis, fertiliser products have made up a “very negligible” share of moving cargo, according to the Washington-based International Food Policy Research Institute.

Moreira da Silva said the UN-backed fertiliser mechanism, drawn up in March, could be activated within seven to 10 days if both Iran and the US agree.

Under the plan, UN monitors would work alongside local authorities at Gulf ports to verify cargo loading. Ships would be tracked during transit, and additional inspections could ⁠be carried out if countries raised concerns about a vessel or its cargo, said Moreira da Silva. He did not say why the US and Iran have not yet agreed.

The passage of only five vessels per day through the Strait of Hormuz could keep fertiliser supplies flowing to countries in critical need, he added.

The UN mechanism could work alongside negotiations for a “comprehensive deal” to restore freedom of navigation in the strait, Moreira da Silva said.

Iran and the US have exchanged proposals through intermediaries since a June interim ceasefire collapsed . Efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have stalled over Tehran’s conditions and Washington’s insistence on addressing Iran’s nuclear programme from the outset.

“What we are telling them is, while you continue your discussions towards a comprehensive deal, let us work, let us do our job,” said Moreira da Silva.

His plea comes amid growing concern that fertiliser shortages could hit global food supplies .

In May, the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization warned that fertiliser scarcity could tighten food supplies from late 2026 into 2027, and would likely hit countries facing climate or other crises much harder.

In South Asia, where most rely on imported fertiliser, farmers are already struggling because of soaring costs and fertiliser scarcity . On Wednesday, farmers in Spain took to the streets to protest rising production costs amid high oil and fertiliser prices.

articles.title: Bullfrogs were brought west for food, hunting and pest control; along Montana's Yellowstone River, their invasion grew from 37 to 66 miles in just 3 years
articles.summary: The American bullfrog population has rapidly expanded along Montana's Yellowstone River, growing from 37 to 66 miles in just three years, raising concerns for local wildlife and habitat balance.
articles.body: American bullfrogs spread along roughly 66 miles of Montana’s Yellowstone River floodplain by 2013, up from about 37 miles in 2010, according to a US Geological Survey report published in October 2014. Researchers also recorded an increase in breeding sites, from 12 to 45 over the same period, and the findings documented a rapidly expanding population of a frog native to eastern North America but introduced to the Yellowstone River region, near Billings, through human activity.People helped bring the frogs to MontanaBullfrogs have been moved beyond their native range for several reasons, including food, recreational hunting, fishing bait and pest control, and some have also been released as unwanted pets. USGS researchers found Yellowstone River bullfrogs at public-access locations with deeper water and emergent vegetation, including ponds and impoundments. Those habitats would have been difficult for the frogs to reach naturally from their eastern North American range, which strengthens the case for human-assisted introduction.The species was first documented in the Yellowstone River floodplain in 1999, and its size, broad diet and ability to reproduce quickly make it a successful coloniser of suitable wetland habitat. The USGS said the 2010, 2012 and 2013 surveys found bullfrogs firmly established in the floodplain and spreading both upstream and downstream. The invasion advanced farther downstream, where river flow could carry animals or their early life stages into additional habitats, and the number of breeding locations also rose sharply during the survey period, which indicated that the population was not simply appearing in new places but reproducing across a wider area.Deeper water provided suitable habitatResearchers searched for adult frogs, egg masses and larvae during field surveys, and also listened for calls from breeding males, travelling by road, on foot and by boat along wetlands and waterways. The frogs were linked with deeper water and emergent vegetation, conditions common in permanent ponds and backwaters, and these findings matter for monitoring because they give land managers a way to prioritise surveys and identify places where new populations may become established.The study was published in the journal Aquatic Invasions, and its authors included scientists from the USGS, Montana Natural Heritage Program, Bureau of Land Management and Montana Fish, Wildlife and Parks. The peer-reviewed paper reported the same increase from roughly 60 kilometres of occupied floodplain in 2010 to 106 kilometres in 2013.Native amphibians could face competitionBullfrogs are large, mobile omnivores that consume a wide range of prey, and their spread has been linked to declines in amphibians and reptiles in other parts of the world, with scientists having raised concerns about competition and predation where bullfrogs overlap with native species.In the Yellowstone River study area, however, the local effects were not yet established when the USGS released its findings, and researchers identified northern leopard frogs as a species of particular concern because their habitat overlaps with that of bullfrogs. The report did not claim that bullfrogs had already caused a measured decline in Yellowstone River leopard frogs, and that difference matters for wildlife management. A rapidly spreading non-native species can present a risk before scientists have enough data to measure its full ecological impact, and monitoring native populations alongside bullfrog numbers is necessary to determine whether those risks are translating into local declines.Researchers tested ways to suppress the populationThe USGS described a separate effort to study bullfrog suppression in the Yellowstone River floodplain in 2016, and examined the distribution of the invasion, its effects on native species and possible control methods, including trapping, seining, dewatering and other removal approaches. The agency noted that bullfrogs can be difficult to eradicate once established because they reproduce prolifically and move readily between habitats.The 2010–2013 survey results provide a historical measure of how quickly the invasion expanded in the study area, but they do not establish the current extent of bullfrogs along the river. The researchers’ work instead identified the habitats and access points where monitoring and prevention could be concentrated.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Fire erupts at Albania’s Education Ministry as protests enter third day
articles.summary: At least 16 additional protesters have been arrested after clashing with riot police.
articles.body:
Protesters started a blaze at Albania’s Education Ministry overnight after a second day of student protests in the country’s capital Tirana that continue unabated.

Demonstrators broke in overnight on Tuesday and lit a fire inside of the building, according to police, adding that the violence resulted in 16 arrests.

Protesters continued to rally on Wednesday. Hundreds of students gathered and slung rocks at the ministry, as they demanded better university conditions and the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama.

In an attempt to break up the crowds, riot police responded with tear gas and water cannons.

Demonstrators also ripped out nearby fencing and used it to block the street.

Hundreds of people rallied on Tuesday in front of the Education Ministry, after fierce protests broke out in Tirana on Monday.

“Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road,” Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook.

“I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!”

Besar Likmeta, editor at the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network in Albania, told Al Jazeera that “this protest came on the back of four months of daily rallies on the main streets of the capital”, known as the “ Flamingo Revolution “.

The movement started in protest of a resort project in a protected area of southern Albania linked to the son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, Jared Kushner .

The project fuelled anger over alleged corruption and a lack of transparency, with protesters demanding Rama’s resignation.

“But then they, they spread into wider demands about better, better opportunities and anti-corruption, lack of opportunities for youth, and particularly a sign of growing disenfranchisement among this younger generation of Albanians,” Likmeta added.

Students told local media that the protests were against university conditions, tuition fees and a lack of support for young people.

articles.body: When professional wrestling stars Mike ‘The Miz’ Mizanin and his wife, Maryse Mizanin, bought a sprawling farmhouse in Austin, Texas, in December 2017, the property offered plenty of room for family life, entertaining and relaxation. With its Mediterranean-inspired architecture, spacious interiors and resort-style outdoor amenities, the house stood out well beyond the wrestling ring.According to the Los Angeles Times, WWE stars The Miz and Maryse bought a new home in California in 2019 after a short stay in Austin, Texas. Their move followed the listing of their 7,770-square-foot Austin farmhouse for $2.75 million in March 2019. They purchased the property in December 2017; it featured a heated infinity-edge swimming pool, a spa, and a bocce ball court.A European-inspired farmhouse with a grand exteriorThis Austin property combined farmhouse design with Mediterranean influences. White stucco walls, arched windows and stone gave the house the look of a luxurious mansion, while its tall ceilings and open interiors made it feel even larger. According to the March 2019 Realtor.com report, the property had five bedrooms, five full bathrooms and five half bathrooms. The interiors of the house included two-story ceilings, stone walls, archways, and a combination of stone, tile and hardwood floors. The kitchen was a focal point, with antique wooden cabinets, a beamed ceiling, and professional appliances.In addition, the house was designed to accommodate visitors and relatives. It included a private suite with its own entrance and kitchenette, while the game room and bar were designed for social gatherings. Overall, the house had the feel of a country retreat with modern conveniences for family living. The house was also tied to the couple’s television careers as Miz and Maryse hosted a television program named Miz & Mrs., which depicted the couple’s private life outside their professional wrestling careers.A backyard built for relaxation and entertainmentSome of the most appealing aspects of the outdoor spaces included the heated negative-edge swimming pool located at the centre. The asking price of $2.75 million was only the beginning of the property’s next chapter. It eventually sold for about $2.64 million in 2019, according to real estate reports. According to the Los Angeles Times, in 2019, the couple bought a much larger property in Thousand Oaks, California, at a price tag of $6.4 million. An English-style manor with approximately 10,400 square feet of living space, six bedrooms, gardens, a swimming pool, a spa, and even a guesthouse.The move marked a shift from their Austin farmhouse, though both homes offered generous indoor and outdoor space. The California property was comparatively large as it included entertainment amenities such as a private movie theatre, a wine cellar, and outdoor entertaining areas. articles.title: Peak Cluster: Fourth council opposes £5bn CO2 pipeline plan
articles.summary: Cheshire East Council votes to object to the carbon capture proposals and write to the government.
articles.body:
Cheshire East Council has become the fourth local authority to formally oppose the proposed Peak Cluster carbon dioxide pipeline.

Councillors unanimously backed a motion calling on the government not to approve the scheme until concerns over safety, environmental impacts and effects on local communities are addressed.

The £5bn project would transport carbon dioxide captured at cement and lime plants in Derbyshire and Staffordshire to storage sites beneath the Irish Sea.

Supporters say it could cut emissions from hard-to-decarbonise industries and protect jobs, while opponents have raised concerns about safety, environmental damage and disruption during construction.

Cheshire East Council joins Derbyshire County Council, Wirral Council and Cheshire West and Chester Council in formally objecting to the proposals.

The motion was brought by Conservative councillors Lesley Smetham and Hayley Whitaker, with independent councillor Michael Gorman and Labour councillor Dawn Clark also supporting an amended version.

It called on the council to formally object to the scheme, submit its concerns to both the developer and the Planning Inspectorate, and ask Peak Cluster representatives to present the proposals directly to councillors.

The motion also called for letters to be sent to government ministers requesting that approval should not be granted until concerns raised by the council had been resolved.

Residents protesting outside the meeting at Tatton Park were joined by a series of public speakers raising concerns about issues including safety, impacts on farming and rural communities, and the overall cost of the scheme.

Presenting the motion, Smetham said tackling climate change was "essential" but argued "we should not do harm during the process".

She described Peak Cluster as a "costly and extreme proposal" and said there was "no benefit" for the people of Cheshire East.

However, Labour councillor Heather Seddon said the scientific case for carbon capture and storage at a national level was "compelling", but argued the local case for the project had yet to be made.

Council leader Nick Mannion also said action was needed on climate change but questioned whether Peak Cluster represented "the safest and most appropriate response for the cement industry".

Last month, Peak Cluster a nnounced changes to parts of the proposed route and reduced the width of the safeguarded pipeline corridor following consultation feedback from more than 5,500 respondents.

A spokesperson for the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero said the government was delivering industrial-scale carbon capture projects that would support jobs and help decarbonise industries such as cement.

The department said sectors including cement were difficult to decarbonise without carbon capture technology, but added that the Peak Cluster project was being developed privately and was not receiving funding from the department.

The motion was approved unanimously by all 66 councillors present.

After the vote, Whitaker said she was pleased councillors had come together on the issue, although she felt it should have reached full council sooner.

Peak Cluster has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Pressing matters: Trump's new spokeswoman struggles on day one
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from Washington: For a White House that treats politics as a television spectacle and television as a political show, Donald Trump's
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: For a White House that treats politics as a television spectacle and television as a political show, Donald Trump's press secretaries have often looked as though they were selected by a casting director rather than the administration’s personnel office. Katie Zacharia arrived at the White House press room lectern on Tuesday camera-ready, with the familiar blonde look that prompted comparisons with Ivanka Trump, which some trolls insist is a required qualification for the job.Then she opened her mouth, made a meal of a $54 billion pipeline, confused her husband with her new boss, answered three questions from favoured media, and made a hasty exit, reminding America that reading the script and performing the job are two very different things. The White House press sec’s post combines the duties of a diplomat, crisis manager, political attack dog, fact-checker and human shock absorber, and the incumbent must know every policy, anticipate every scandal, explain every presidential improvisation and survive questions about things the president may have said five minutes earlier — or deny saying five years ago. She’s not there yet.Her opening intonation of Trump achievements -- from jobs and drug prices to oil deals and naval construction -- evoked comparisons to a malfunctioning voice assistant, with the Guardian dubbing her the “Zachbot,” and other critics likening it to a comedy sketch. But the line destined to outlive her tenure came during a discussion of family life. Explaining that she did not intend to sacrifice time with her four children, Zacharia began: “So my president — excuse me, my husband...”To be fair, a slip of the tongue is hardly a constitutional crisis. Every politician has mangled a sentence, none more than Donald Trump, and the briefing room has witnessed considerably worse than a momentary matrimonial mix-up. Most press secs barrel on, but Zacharia instead appeared to decide that the safest answer to a difficult briefing was to stop having one.The reviews were harsh. Aaron Rupar, a journalist who tracks political video, quipped that Zacharia made her predecessor Karoline Leavitt look like Winston Churchill. Another compared her reading level with that of a third-grader -- or just above Trump. Even allowing for the customary partisan relish with which Washington grades the other side’s performances, the consensus was that this was not the sort of debut that inspires confidence.Trump, naturally, offered a different assessment, saying he thought she was “very good.” Presidential approval, after all, is the one review that matters most in this particular workplace. But disaster struck when questions arose about where she passed the bar exam, after she was described as a lawyer. "When I moved to China…” she responded, standing behind Trump in a media gaggle outside the White House. That triggered another cascade of jokes, with one late-nighter quipping, “Even Trump’s press secretary is Made in China.”On a more serious note, it emerged that she has a law degree from Pepperdine (2011) and worked as an associate at Zhong Lun, a Beijing law firm (2011–2013). Critics were quick to pounce on it, pointing out that working at a Chinese firm as a foreign law graduate is not the same as being licensed to practice law. Her answers do not establish that she passed a bar exam anywhere, and therefore she cannot call herself a lawyer.What she has passed with flying colours, though, is in the field of conspiracy theories, which she has parlayed aplenty as a MAGA megaphone on TV and social media. And while she has already mastered the MAGA media ecosystem, where a conspiracy theory can be promoted to established fact before the next commercial break, the White House briefing room is less forgiving: the questions are live, the follow-ups are real, and the exit is not always available on demand.For now, though, Trump is happy, the internet is entertained, and the press corps has a new source of material. Going forward, Zacharia's task is to persuade the world that she is more than a blonde wig, a stack of talking points and a voice assistant that is still buffering.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sally Rooney’s publisher withdraws her books from U.K. sale over support for Palestine Action
articles.summary: Irish novelist Sally Rooney said on Wednesday that her books are being withdrawn from sale in the U.K. because of her support for Palestine Action, a protest group the British government has outlawed as a terrorist organization.
articles.body: LONDON — Irish novelist Sally Rooney said on Wednesday that her books are being withdrawn from sale in the U.K. because of her support for Palestine Action, a protest group the British government has outlawed as a terrorist organization. Her publisher, Faber, confirmed that the ban “has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on U.K. earnings to Sally Rooney for her work.” “To sell a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher. As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the U.K. in any format,” Faber said in a statement. Rooney said Faber’s decision to withdraw her books from sale in the U.K. was made “with my full agreement.” “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions, and I am wholly prepared to accept the consequences,” she said in a statement. Rooney, 35, is the critically praised author of four novels: “Conversations with Friends,” “Normal People,” “Beautiful World, Where are You” and “Intermezzo.” Her books have sold millions of copies, and both “Conversations with Friends” and “Normal People” were adapted for television by the BBC. A strong supporter of Palestinian causes, she wrote in The Irish Times in August 2025: “I too support Palestine Action. If this makes me a ‘supporter of terror’ under U.K. law, so be it.” She said she would use proceeds from her novels and TV fees to continue to support the group. Britain’s center-left Labour government outlawed Palestine Action after activists from the direct-action group broke into a Royal Air Force base in June 2025 to protest British military support for Israel’s military offensive in Gaza. The ban makes membership in or support for the group a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison. More than 3,000 people have been arrested since the group was outlawed, including for holding signs declaring “I support Palestine Action.” More than 1,200 have been charged under the Terrorism Act, though none has yet been convicted. Civil liberties groups say the ban and subsequent arrests unjustifiably restrict the rights to protest and free speech. Lawyers for Palestine Action will ask the U.K. Supreme Court next month to overturn the ban. All cases involving people charged with breaching it have been put on hold pending the court’s ruling.

articles.title: Gift for Putin as fears grow that Trump is turning the screws on Ukraine
articles.summary: Ultimately, you have to wonder what it is that Vladimir Putin says to Donald Trump when they are on the phone.
articles.body: Ultimately, you have to wonder what it is that Vladimir Putin says to Donald Trump when they are on the phone. A week ago, a call between the US president and his Russian counterpart seemed to be about an urgent clarification over a possible outbreak of plague in Siberia. Instead, a controversial deal to buy Russian diesel emerged, prompting fury from Ukrainians, and then Trump demanding they get a new president. For days, fears grew across Europe this may spill into the real world of the US limiting military aid and intelligence for Ukraine, and in the past 48 hours, that might be spilling into reality. Twice now, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky has declared Kyiv was not given the usual warning about Russian ballistic missile attacks from its partners. The US, whose satellites and other methods are the early warning mechanisms for Russian launches, normally provide Ukrainians a vital few minutes to run to the shelter before the missiles hit. Thirty-nine slammed into Ukraine last night. President Trump has openly rejected the idea he has stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine, saying Tuesday: “We are helping them, and we are sharing intel.” But that does not preclude the possibility less intelligence is being shared, or it is less in real time. With the dead from Russian strikes often in the dozens, as Moscow seeks to yet further widen the envelope of what civilian carnage it will impose, a sudden withdrawal of these early warnings would mean many Ukrainians will likely die. It is possible there is another reason for Zelensky’s messaging – that he is pre-emptively posturing, or that poor weather or technical issues prompted the lack of warnings. The second withdrawal of assistance that appeared to beset Ukraine Wednesday also suggests Trump is squeezing them harder. Starlink space-based internet antennae – assisting Ukrainian medium and longer-range drones to hit their targets, and interceptors to tackle Russian loitering drones – have had significant speed limits imposed on them. This may amount to the removal of a bonus capability negotiated by the former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov with Space X’s owner, Elon Musk. It is important to note it is not comparable to Musk’s decision to entirely stop Starlink functioning inside Russia, which significantly hampered Moscow’s frontline operations in the summer of last year. But it is a palpable snub with operational significance, and one that Ukrainian officials have said would only have occurred at the behest of the White House. For days, European and Ukrainian officials have warned the US was threatening to limit intelligence and other cooperation if Kyiv did not stop hitting Russian diesel facilities. Trump has – somewhat misleadingly – stated Ukrainian targeting of Moscow’s oil facilities is behind a surge in pump prices in the United States, choosing to ignore the role the Strait of Hormuz has played in this global economic calamity. It is possible the Starlink slowdown and lack of ballistic warnings shows this threat coming to life. President Trump has denied this is the case, but that is not in of itself definitive proof it is not happening. Trump has also – since he spoke to Putin – again swung from deciding to finally allow Ukraine to build its own Patriot interceptors, a high-profile and vital move long-prevaricated over, to deciding the true obstacle to peace is Zelensky, the president of the invaded country, who has been asking for an immediate ceasefire for over a year. It does not appear to influence Trump’s thought process when Putin attacks Ukrainian energy facilities in the middle of Trump’s self-declared “energy ceasefire.” Or when Putin’s operatives plot to murder a dissident in Washington DC. Or when US businesses are relentlessly hit in Ukraine. There are moments when Trump simply appears bent on hurting Ukraine and damaging its position. We may never learn why, or what it is that Putin says to him to cause this relatively frequent flip in Trump’s worldview. Conjecture might revive the old trope that Trump the real-estate dealmaker seeks to pressure his subcontractors (here, Ukraine) to get the deal to go through or forge a price more palatable to his end consumer (Putin), who he has correctly assessed is in the driving seat of the war and therefore any peace deal. But the timing of this pressure rarely comes when a deal is close, or appears supported by logic. Trump’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel, by most analysis, won’t impact prices at the American pump before the mid-terms, but will likely flood the Kremlin’s coffers with badly needed cash. Zelensky and his European allies have seen this vacillation enough times to be inured to its emotional impact, and perhaps even relaxed about how long it might sustain. Perhaps more Trump-whispering by France’s Macron, or another call from NATO’s Rutte, or visit from Italy’s Meloni, will see the US president flip back again. Indeed, Zelensky was in London Wednesday, and the topic has surely come up. But Trump’s persistent sympathy for Russia’s position remains a mystery of our time. Critics say it is unlikely to achieve his apparent goal of a peace deal, incompatible with the long-term security interests of the United States, and oblivious to Moscow’s role in assisting Iran , which continues to embarrass Trump and injure American servicemen. There is an inherent risk in the current state of affairs, however, to both Trump and Putin. First, Trump might create such acrimony in his transatlantic relationships, that his allies simply zone him out for the 18 months after the mid-terms, and wait for him to depart. That could leave Trump further hamstrung when dealing with an intractable conflict, spreading in the Middle East. There is risk for Putin too. Europe and Ukraine being forced to forge ahead without the United States, fashion resilience, find new methods, and surge funding into their defense, does not leave the Kremlin in a dominant position. The more Moscow antagonizes Europe, the more it arms up, and the greater, in the long-term, the (defensive) threat Europe’s armies pose to Russia. Ukraine has shown extraordinary inventiveness and capability. That is unlikely to stop, and likely to again reshape the landscape of warfare in the coming years. Similarly, Russia’s capacity to absorb pain is immense. Yet its breaking point is rarely publicly visible, and tends to surge menacingly from the deep without warning, as when the frustrated chief of Russia’s infamous Wagner mercenary force launched a short-lived rebellion in 2023. In the immediate term however, the risk of this current strategy is born entirely by Ukraine. Its children and mothers are dying from nightly strikes. Its cities are sleepless. And its military aid is prey to two powerful men’s curious bromance.

articles.title: Mosqitter is turning its mosquito traps into an AI-powered surveillance network | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Mosqitter is turning its mosquito-trapping hardware into an AI-powered surveillance network designed to identify species, monitor populations, and provide earlier warnings of mosquito-borne disease risks.
articles.body:
Mosquitoes and the diseases they carry are expanding into new territory. Rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and global travel are reshaping where disease-carrying mosquitoes can thrive, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Cases of dengue, a viral illness spread by mosquito bites, more than doubled in a year, from 6.5 million reported globally in 2023 to a record 14.6 million in 2024, the WHO says.

A 30-person, Pennsylvania-based startup, Mosqitter , thinks fighting that problem requires more than killing mosquitoes. The company started by building chemical-free devices that lure and trap female mosquitoes by mimicking the heat, scent, and breathing cues of humans.

Anastasiia Romanova, co-founder and CEO of Mosqitter, told TechCrunch that the company set out to bring more sustainable mosquito-control products to a market still heavily reliant on chemicals. Romanova says it now has more than 5,000 devices operating across five continents, up from just over 250 when TechCrunch last covered the company in 2022. The startup now wants to turn its traps into an AI-powered monitoring network that can identify mosquito species, track changes in their numbers, and give earlier warnings about emerging disease risks.

Mosqitter began its R&D in Ukraine in 2019 and launched business operations in 2021, which the company considers its official go-to-market year. The company started by examining mosquito behavior. Female mosquitoes, the only ones that bite, seek blood before laying eggs. They lay eggs on a roughly three-week cycle, typically 100 to 200 at a time.

“We saw an opportunity: If we could catch the female mosquito at the point when she is about to lay eggs, we could potentially reduce the mosquito population and prevent it from growing,” Romanova said. “That’s why we combined elements such as heat, similar to the temperature of human skin; scent that imitates human skin odor; and light. In the Grand model,” which is the company’s highest-end offering, “we also use CO 2 to imitate human breathing.”

Mosqitter, presenting Wednesday as part of TechCrunch’s storied Startup Battlefield competition happening this week in downtown San Francisco, is using AI to identify the mosquitoes its devices catch. Its computer-vision system analyzes biological characteristics to distinguish between species, Romanova told TechCrunch.

To identify a mosquito, Mosqitter runs an image through its neural network, checks the result against external datasets, and has entomologists validate the findings. It then assigns a confidence score based on how closely those assessments align.

“You can think about it as three judges analyzing a case and producing a verdict,” Romanova said.

Mosqitter also feeds environmental data, including weather, wind, and humidity, into its system. The company says that as it collects more data, it plans to use those inputs to forecast changes in mosquito populations and potential health risks.

Mosqitter’s product portfolio currently centers on two devices. Mosqitter Grand, its flagship product, is designed for larger areas and public spaces, while Mosqitter Mini targets smaller residential spaces and can also be deployed as a portable monitoring device. The startup plans to officially introduce its Febris Monitoring System next month, adding a data layer to monitor mosquito populations and assess the potential spread of mosquito-borne diseases.

“It’s very important to understand that Febris does not diagnose disease,” Romanova said. “We can’t say with certainty that a particular mosquito carries dengue. What we can say is that a particular mosquito species is present, and knowing that can help indicate an increased potential risk associated with diseases that species can transmit.”

The company is looking for B2B partners globally, particularly distributors with established sales networks and relationships with governments and retailers, Olga Diachuk, COO and co-founder of Mosqitter, said. Unlike Mosqitter’s hardware products, Febris targets institutional customers, including governments, public-health and mosquito-control agencies, airports, municipalities, and universities that need continuous mosquito monitoring.

Brazil, which has a high burden of dengue , is one example of Mosqitter’s expansion. Mosqitter has built local manufacturing and sales operations there, according to the co-founders. The startup also considers the U.S., Greece, India, Ukraine, and Nigeria key markets, and it uses a different sales approach in each.

In Greece, Mosqitter works with a long-established pest-control company. In the U.S., it sells its Mini device directly to consumers through Amazon and its own website. The company is also working with the U.K. Health Security Agency to deploy Febris at locations including Heathrow and Gatwick airports. International travel can bring in mosquitoes and mosquito-borne diseases from other regions, and Romanova says this highlights the need for more continuous monitoring.

“We think this part of the business could grow substantially with the Febris Monitoring System because governments are major buyers of mosquito-surveillance data,” Romanova said.

Mosqitter Mini retails for $199, while its professional Grand system costs $1,999. The company makes money from hardware sales, while Febris adds a recurring revenue stream from monitoring, dashboards, analytics, and data services.

Mosqitter is on track to generate more than $1 million in revenue in 2026, Romanova said. Revenue from Febris has only recently started coming in, but the company projects the data business could bring in more than $3.5 million next year, based on the value of contracts it is currently bidding on.

Mosqitter is raising a $5 million round in two tranches, starting with $1 million and followed by another $4 million. The startup said the split is tied to milestones it plans to reach with its Febris Monitoring System. To date, Mosqitter has raised $1.9 million.

There’s also a story behind the name. Despite what most people assume, “Mosqitter” isn’t a mashup of “mosquito” and “quitter,” Diachuk said. It combines “mosquito” and “eater,” a name that made more sense when the company was focused primarily on catching mosquitoes.

Julie Hanway Molina, 56, is charged with four counts of wire fraud. It alleges that from 2023 to November 2025, Molina carried out a scheme to defraud the nonprofit. She diverted money from the group's bank account for personal expenses without the organisation's knowledge or authorisation, including her home mortgage and credit card bills. In total, the Justice Department said, she misappropriated approximately $411,761 belonging to the nonprofit.As CBS LA reported, prosecutors allege Molina took the money in her role as treasurer and that the funds were diverted from the booster club's bank account. It gave the same total of about $411,761 and attributed its account to the Department of Justice. The US Attorney's Office also stated that an indictment is merely an allegation and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.How did the California booster club treasurer allegedly conceal the $411,761 fraudThe Justice Department said that in June 2023, Molina wired approximately $131,523 from the nonprofit's bank account in Laguna Hills to an account in Santa Ana. The figure was more than $131,000 and reported the same route and destination. Prosecutors also allege that Molina tried to conceal the payments. articles.title: Kenya’s Health Ministry confirms second Ebola case
articles.summary: A relative of the first case, 39-year-old man’s infection raises concerns of a cross-border spread.
articles.body:
Kenya has reported a second Ebola infection, about a week after confirming its first-ever case of the disease when a citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) travelled to Kenya and died two days later at a Nairobi hospital.

The second patient, a 39-year-old man who is a close family member of the first case, fell ill on Tuesday and was already in quarantine when he came down with symptoms of fever, fatigue and joint pain, the Ministry of Health said in a statement Wednesday.

Last week’s case raised concerns about deficiencies in border screening systems in the region after the patient drove from the DRC to Uganda and flew to Nairobi from there.

Given the closure of the border between the DRC and Uganda since May because of the outbreak of the virus, it is not clear how he was able to enter the country.

Alan Kasujja, executive director of the Ugandan government’s media centre, questioned how Kenya allowed the man to enter via its airport.

“Leave Uganda out of this conversation. We don’t have Ebola here,” he wrote on X.

When asked how the patient was able to travel through three countries undetected, Kenya’s Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said last week that a meeting was scheduled with officials from the DRC and Uganda and the Africa CDC to investigate.

Kenya has intensified its national response to the disease since the country recorded the first case. At the time, Kenya traced everyone who came in contact with the patient and reported at least 57 people, with 10 immediately quarantined, Health Minister Aden Duale told journalists on October 7.

Kenya is the fourth country to record a case linked to the Ebola epidemic in the DRC, the second-largest on record globally with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.

Uganda reported 20 cases and two deaths earlier in the year but was declared Ebola-free in August. A doctor who returned to France in June from the DRC tested positive, but there was no further spread of the virus.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of infected people, whether living or dead. The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhoea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding.

The second patient is currently at a designated treatment centre, where he is receiving the appropriate care, the Health Ministry said. It will continue to share information on his progress, the ministry added.

articles.title: Pope shares first message after lung cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV thanked fellow Catholics for their prayers on Wednesday in his first message since he underwent surgery for lung cancer in Rome.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV thanked fellow Catholics for their prayers on Wednesday in his first message since he underwent surgery for lung cancer in Rome. “As you know, I have been unable to be among you during these days,” Leo wrote in a statement to Catholics participating in a symposium for the 10th anniversary of Amoris laetitia, a document written by his predecessor Pope Francis on the church’s work with couples and families. “I thank you warmly for your prayers and for the work you have done together. Your sharing of experiences and attentive listening are indeed a gift to the whole Church,” he said. “I ask you please to pray for me, as I pray for you.” Leo was diagnosed with pulmonary adenocarcinoma, a common type of lung cancer, during a 90-minute surgery in Rome yesterday wherein doctors removed the lower lobe of one of his lungs, according to medical staff who treated the pontiff. The pope’s recovery is “proceeding as expected,” Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Stefano Margaritora said in their statement. Leo was able to walk around his quarters in the hospital and ate breakfast and lunch. The pope announced his planned surgery in a speech over the weekend to faithful in St. Peter’s Square, saying that the “growth” on his lung was found at an early stage. The pope isn’t known to be a smoker and has made efforts to have a healthy lifestyle, but there is a history of cancer in his immediate family. His older brother Louis Prevost is currently in treatment for cancer, and their parents died of the disease in the 1990s. Pope Leo has cancelled all his public appearances until October 20 in light of his treatment, though he is due to embark on a long trip to South America next month.

articles.title: Sally Rooney’s books no longer sold in UK over support for banned pro-Palestinian group
articles.summary: Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine ​Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and ‌her publisher said on Wednesday.
articles.body: Irish novelist Sally Rooney’s books will no longer be sold in Britain over her plans to use her royalties to support Palestine ​Action, a pro-Palestinian group banned as a terrorist organisation, Rooney and ‌her publisher said on Wednesday. The bestselling author, known for novels including “Normal People” and “Conversations with Friends,” has been a vocal supporter of Palestine Action, including after it was proscribed by ​the British government under terrorism laws last year. Rooney previously said in ​a witness statement submitted to London’s High Court, in support of ⁠a legal challenge over the ban on Palestine Action, that her plans ​could lead to her books being withdrawn from sale in Britain. Her publisher Faber ​said on Wednesday that it had agreed with Rooney that “we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format,” though it would sell her works elsewhere. “Current ​legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass ​on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work,” Faber said in a statement. “To sell ‌a ⁠writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher.” Rooney said in a statement: “I have made every effort to be honest with the public about my beliefs and intentions and I ​am wholly prepared to ​accept the ⁠consequences.” Palestine Action, which had increasingly targeted Israel-linked defense companies, was banned shortly after a June 2025 break-in at the ​Royal Air Force’s Brize Norton base. Last year, Palestine Action’s co-founder ​Huda Ammori ⁠challenged the ban and the High Court ruled in her favor in February, before the Court of Appeal overturned that decision in June. The Supreme Court is due ⁠to ​hear an appeal next month. More than 3,000 people ​have since been arrested for holding signs in support of Palestine Action and its proscription has ​been criticized by civil liberties groups.

articles.title: We are behind you and that will not change, PM tells Zelensky
articles.summary: The Ukrainian president visited London in an effort to bolster support among European allies following a row with Donald Trump.
articles.body:
"We are behind you and that will not change," Andy Burnham has told Volodymyr Zelensky, as he hosted the Ukrainian leader in Downing Street.

Zelensky was in London as part of efforts to reinforce backing from allies after Donald Trump called for him to go and lifted sanctions on Russian diesel.

The prime minister said Ukraine was willing to discuss an energy ceasefire proposed by the US president but said Russia's response had been "further attacks on critical national infrastructure in Ukraine".

Zelensky said: "Our people, we survived and continue to do this because we have strong partners and I'm very proud that we have one of the strongest partners in our history and it's your people, Andy."

The Ukrainian president was greeted with a hug from Burnham, cheers from civil servants and a rare honour guard as he arrived in Downing Street.

Ahead of Zelensky's arrival, No 10 announced it would speed up delivery of lightweight multirole missiles to Ukraine, which have been used to bring down Russian drones.

Ukrainian officials have said that overnight strikes by Russian missiles and drones had left at least 600,000 people without electricity.

For the second consecutive night, Ukraine said it had not received advanced warning from its allies of a wave of missile strikes coming from Russia.

Zelensky has suggested the US had threatened to restrict intelligence-sharing unless he agreed to sign up to an energy ceasefire. Trump has denied the US is holding back information.

Speaking in Downing Street, Burnham said the recent days had been "dark and difficult" for Ukraine, with the country suffering "heavy bombardment".

He told the Ukrainian leader: "You have seen the solidarity and the support you have got from everybody here in Britain.

"We are behind you and that will not change."

Earlier in the day, Burnham had been invited to criticise the US decision to lift sanctions on Russia, when, at Prime Minister's Questions, Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey asked if the PM agreed there had been a "shameful Trump betrayal".

Burnham acknowledged that Zelensky was "carrying the heaviest of weights" but avoided attacking Trump, instead telling MPs that his role was to "repair bridges so that the support comes back".

"Therefore I should, at this moment in time, be careful in terms of laying the ground to bring people back together."

He added that Zelensky would not come away from his trip "empty-handed".

On Friday, Trump shocked European allies when he announced that he had reached a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel, with more to follow.

Concerns about the cost of living are playing a key part in the US's November elections and the US president hopes his deal with Russia will reduce the cost of diesel.

The agreement runs counter to sanctions imposed on Russia by the US and its allies in a bid to choke off funds for Putin's war in Ukraine.

The deal came days after Trump accused Zelensky of wanting to "make problems for the world" and that it was time for Ukraine to "get a new president".

The criticism marks a renewal of Trump's previous hostility towards Zelensky which resulted in an infamous public row between the two men in the Oval Office.

articles.title: Do you actually need pet laundry detergent to clean your dog’s things?
articles.summary: Pet laundry detergents are on the rise, but are they different from regular detergent? Veterinarians explain whether your dog or cat really needs it.
articles.body: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans. Between muddy paws, drool, and the occasional accident, your dog’s bed, blankets, and toys can get dirty fast. And if you’ve shopped for laundry supplies lately, you may have noticed a growing number of detergents made specifically for pets, with promises to tackle odors and stains while being gentler on your dog’s skin. But are they actually any different from the detergent you already use? Most of us aren’t looking to add another expense to our bills for household essentials. So I spoke to two veterinarians to find out what sets pet laundry detergents apart from regular ones, and which ones are the best if you find that you should be using one of these formulas to clean your furry friend’s things. What is pet laundry detergent? Pet laundry detergent is exactly what it sounds like: detergent sold with your pet’s things in mind. “Pet laundry detergents are products marketed specifically for washing things pets use, such as bedding, blankets, crate pads, washable toys, towels, and clothing,” says Dr. Jo Myers, a veterinarian at Vetster, a pet telehealth company. That doesn’t mean your dog’s bed needs its own special soap, though. “Pet laundry detergent is more of a marketing term than a necessity, and most pets do not need a detergent specifically formulated for them,” says Dr. Liza Cahn, veterinarian at Embrace Pet Insurance. “If owners do choose a pet-specific product, one potential benefit is that it may contain enzymes or other ingredients designed to break down pet-related stains and odors, which can be especially useful for washing bedding, towels, and toys.” The best laundry detergents for pets If you decide a pet-specific formula is right for your household, there are plenty of options to choose from. To help narrow them down, I rounded up highly-rated pet laundry detergents. Each made-for-pets detergent in this list is designed to tackle the stains and odors that come with washing your dog’s (or cat’s) bedding, blankets, and toys. NBC Selected editors also shared the detergents they use for their pets below. This powder detergent uses enzymes to break down pet urine, sweat, oils, and other protein-based stains, the kind of formula Cahn says can be especially useful for bedding, towels, and toys. It’s designed to neutralize stubborn stenches like wet dog smell, and it works in standard and high-efficiency washers. A 2-pound bag handles up to 64 loads, according to the brand, so even though it’s a bit pricey it should last you a while. This detergent is a triple-concentrated, low-sudsing liquid that’s safe for high-efficiency washers, and the brand says it tackles tough odors, stains, and heavy soils. A 64-ounce jug handles up to 96 washes, so depending on how often you wash your fur babies’ things, you’ll likely have it for several months. This liquid detergent uses a blend of enzymes to lift stains and odors that come from urine, feces, blood, saliva, and vomit. It’s free of dyes and fragrance, the type of formula Myers says the Center for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) suggests for pets with sensitive skin. It also comes in a lightly scented version and they both work in high-efficiency washers. You’ll need 1 to 2 ounces for a regular-size load, so this 32-ounce bottle may not last as long as some of the others on this list. This isn’t a detergent on its own but an additive you pour in with your regular detergent. It’s designed to remove tough pet odors from beds, blankets, carriers, and collars in a single wash, according to the brand, and it works in standard and high-efficiency washers. You only need no more than a capful for light odors, so unless you have a furry friend who gets into really stinky things, this 98-ounce bottle will last a long time. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans uses this detergent for her entire family, including her 3-year-old silky terrier Minni. “Thankfully she doesn’t shed, but she does start to smell like a corn chip factory between baths. Every time I bathe her, I wash her blankets, harnesses, bedding and favorite toys in this,” she says. “I’ve never had an issue getting odors out — though, she is only 7 pounds. I just love that she isn’t particularly sensitive, so I don’t need to invest in anything outside of what we already buy.” Evans does have a bag of Active Pet Laundry Detergent that she got from a colleague to test. “If ever there’s a smell or stain that my tried-and-true won’t remove, I’m switching to this,” she says. I recently switched my entire family over to this laundry detergent — including my 7-year-old French bulldog, Myko. It’s gentle enough for my kids, as well as Myko’s sensitive skin. French bulldogs are notoriously prone to allergies and Myko frequently has little red patches of irritation. The last thing I want is lingering detergent on her favorite blanket or harness to further inflame her skin. This detergent is free of chemicals, but still manages to get out gross pet odors, stains and more. What is the difference between pet detergent and regular laundry detergent? Despite the special labels, pet laundry detergents may not be all that different from what’s already in your laundry room. “Veterinary hospitals have been washing enormous quantities of animal bedding for a very long time without requiring a special category of pet detergent,” says Myers. “Based on the evidence we currently have, I wouldn’t tell pet owners they need a special detergent simply because the laundry belongs to their pet.” In fact, public health guidance points to the detergent you already own. “The CDC’s guidance on cleaning and disinfecting pet supplies specifically recommends ordinary laundry detergent for machine-washing soft pet items and says it’s okay to wash pet items with your clothes,” says Myers. “For pets described as having sensitive skin, the CDC says detergent without dyes or fragrance may be a good choice.” So if your dog’s skin is easily irritated, a free-and-clear formula, whether or not it’s labeled for pets, may be the better pick. We also ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. I am a commerce editor at NBC Selected and a journalist who regularly covers wellness, beauty, home and lifestyle. I have written about how often you should wash your makeup brushes, portable washing machines and more. I am also a dog mom to Myko, my 7-year-old French Bulldog, who has very sensitive skin. For this story, I interviewed two veterinarians on how pet laundry detergents differ from regular detergent. articles.title: In 2000, Bill Clinton created California's Giant Sequoia National Monument after logging threatened groves; 328,000 acres were protected
articles.summary: Discover how President Bill Clinton established California's Giant Sequoia National Monument in 2000 to protect valuable sequoia groves from commercial logging. Learn about the monument's significance and the ongoing challenges facing these ancient trees.
articles.body: President Bill Clinton created California's Giant Sequoia National Monument on April 15, 2000, and protected approximately 327,769 acres of federal land in the southern Sierra Nevada. The monument included 34 giant sequoia groves and surrounding forest, at a time when many of the groves outside national parks were exposed to commercial logging.Clinton used the Antiquities Act to withdraw the federal acreage from activities including new mining claims and commercial timber disposition, and the proclamation said that the protected area was the smallest area that would be considered compatible with caring for the scientific, historic, and ecological resources identified in the order. Giant sequoias already had substantial protection inside Sequoia, Kings Canyon and Yosemite National Parks by 2000, and the problem was that many other groves stood on national forest land, where surrounding forest could still be managed for timber.Logging had already reached some sequoia grovesPBS SoCal's account of the monument's creation states that more than 9,000 acres of giant-sequoia groves had been logged before the monument was designated, and environmental groups and other advocates campaigned for stronger protection as timber harvesting continued in parts of the Sequoia National Forest.Giant sequoias grow naturally only along a narrow section of California's Sierra Nevada, and the U.S. Forest Service currently estimates roughly 65 to 75 natural groves, depending on how groves are defined. The species occupies a relatively small geographic range, with the larger concentration of groves in the southern Sierra Nevada, and Clinton's administration described the new monument as protecting 34 groves and the forest around them. At the time, the White House said those groves represented a substantial share of the remaining giant sequoia population.The monument did not close the forest to visitorsClinton’s proclamation directed the Forest Service to maintain public and recreational access, including hiking, camping, hunting, fishing, horseback riding, and other activities. Current grazing permits and special-use authorizations could also continue under existing rules, motorized vehicles were restricted to designated roads, and the proclamation barred new roads or trails unless they served the monument’s protective purposes. It also allowed a limited number of timber sales already covered by existing contracts to be completed, with the White House saying that those sales would provide a transition period of about two and a half years before commercial timber harvesting ended within the monument. The proclamation also required the Agriculture Department to prepare a management plan within three years and establish a scientific advisory board to guide on issues including fire management.The monument covered more than the trees themselvesThe 2000 proclamation included surrounding conifer forests, meadows, granite formations, caves and other ecological and geological features, with the monument stretching across elevations from roughly 2,500 to 9,700 feet and covering a varied landscape around the groves. Commercial timber harvesting was not treated as the primary purpose of the monument, and the Forest Service was directed to manage the area under the new protective designation, and existing recreational access and certain other uses could continue under the terms of the proclamation. Contemporary reporting described the protected groves as containing about two-thirds of the world's remaining giant sequoias, not two-thirds of all sequoia groves. The 34 groves themselves represented about half of the roughly 70 groves then identified in the Sierra Nevada. PBS SoCal account of the monument's creationGiant sequoias remain exposed to wildfire, drought and changing forest conditions, and the Forest Service continues to manage the monument as part of the Sequoia National Forest. The 2000 decision established the large protected area; it did not remove the need for ongoing forest management.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Albania’s capital, Tirana, witnessed a fresh outbreak of violence on Wednesday as student protesters clashed with police, vehicles burned and the Education Ministry caught fire during demonstrations over education costs, university conditions and alleged government corruption.Police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds, as the student-led protests fed into a broader anti-government movement demanding the resignation of prime minister Edi Rama.Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside the Education Ministry, with some throwing bricks at the building, breaking metal sidewalk barriers and overturning bins, according to Reuters footage.A nearby Raiffeisen Bank branch also caught fire, a Reuters witness said. Videos circulating from the protests showed burning vehicles and demonstrators dressed in black taking to the streets.The unrest entered its second day on Wednesday after a student rally turned violent late Tuesday. Protesters smashed shop windows and erected street barricades using burning rubbish bins, while riot police moved to disperse the crowds. Police said 23 people were detained overnight, with six officers and one journalist injured.Students cite education costs, inequalityStudent organisers said the demonstrations were driven by concerns over university conditions, the rising cost of higher education, financial support and employment prospects after graduation. Some protesters also voiced anger over inequality and the widening gap between rich and poor.Although the demonstrations began with grievances over public education, students later joined the so-called Flamingo anti-government movement, which has called for Rama’s resignation over allegations of widespread corruption.Deputy prime minister Albana Koçiu criticised the destruction of public property while acknowledging the right to protest."Violence has not been, is not, and will never be a solution. Throwing stones, attacking institutions and the state police, as well as the senseless destruction of public property, are not how youth should express themselves," Koçiu wrote on Facebook.She added: "Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road." She also urged students and citizens to "Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!"The latest clashes mark the most violent escalation of anti-corruption protests that began in May, increasing pressure on Rama’s government. The demonstrations also come amid student activism elsewhere in Europe, including weeks of school blockades in France over staffing shortages and deteriorating facilities.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Shocked': Odisha governor's 'will work for BJP' remark sparks political row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Odisha's newly appointed Governor Braj Mohan Ram has triggered a political row after reportedly saying he would work to strengthen the BJP,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Odisha's newly appointed Governor Braj Mohan Ram has triggered a political row after reportedly saying he would work to strengthen the BJP, drawing sharp criticism from the opposition Biju Janata Dal (BJD) and Congress on Wednesday. Both parties said the remarks raised questions about the impartiality expected of a constitutional office-holder. The Congress demanded that Ram be recalled, while BJD president Naveen Patnaik urged him to uphold constitutional dignity.The BJD shared a PTI video in which Ram was heard speaking about his plans after taking charge as governor. Reacting to the remarks, the party said it was shocked and accused him of undermining the principle that a governor must remain above party politics.“We are shocked to hear his comments in a PTI video, where he reiterates that he would work towards strengthening the BJP. We condemn the remark as it negates the fact that the governor is above party politics,” the BJD said in a statement.Naveen Patnaik hopes governor will uphold constitutional dignityPatnaik, the leader of the opposition in the Odisha Assembly, also expressed concern over the reported remarks. In a social media post, he referred to the governor's enthusiasm for party work and hoped he would discharge his constitutional responsibilities impartially."The people of Odisha are witnessing the enthusiasm of the nominated Governor for undertaking party work. Hope that Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath will bestow upon him the zeal and strength to serve the people of Odisha, through which he will fulfil his duties impartially while upholding constitutional dignity,“ the leader of the opposition in the Odisha Assembly said in a social media post.He tagged Rashtrapati Bhavan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in the post.BJD media coordinator Lenin Mohanty also criticised the comments, calling them unbecoming of a governor.Congress seeks governor's recallThe Congress accused Ram of openly expressing a partisan position before assuming a constitutional office. Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee (OPCC) president Bhakta Charan Das said the governor's role was to protect the Constitution rather than advance a political party's interests.“The Governor’s constitutional responsibility is to uphold the Constitution impartially, not to advance the electoral interests of any political party."Das said constitutional offices must remain above partisan politics. He alleged that Ram had stated he would work for the BJP's SC Morcha in Odisha, as he had done in Jharkhand in the past."It is extremely unfortunate for someone holding the dignified office of Governor to say that he will work to boost the BJP's vote share in Odisha. This exposes the true nature of the BJP," he said."The BJP government is systematically bringing one constitutional institution after another under the party's control. However, no one has ever engaged in such open partisan politics prior to assuming such a high office,” the OPCC leader said.OPCC spokesperson Arabinda Das demanded that the Centre immediately recall Ram. Alternatively, he said, the chief justice of the High Court should raise objections to administering the oath of office to him.Mahua Moitra takes a swipe at BJPTrinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra also joined the criticism, taking a sarcastic dig at Ram and the BJP in a post on X.“Hello Odisha- this is your new governor. He says his job is to strengthen saffron organisation in Odisha. The state has become a dump yard for unemployed senior sanghis! @Naveen_Odisha”.Ram, a three-time former BJP MP, was appointed Odisha governor on Monday. The Odisha BJP had not responded to the reported remarks at the time of publication.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Despite revenue dept push, prohibited property lists yet to be updated
articles.summary: Telangana’s prohibited property (22A) lists on IGRS remain outdated despite govt promises, leaving landowners stuck as districts delay revisions and uploads.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Two months after the state govt promised time-bound relief on prohibited properties, many landowners are still waiting for action. While several long-pending land issues have been resolved, allegations are mounting that district administrations, particularly in the Hyderabad metropolitan region, have been slow to revise and upload updated prohibited property lists, leaving thousands of applicants in limbo.In Aug, revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy had assured that pending applications related to prohibited properties in the core urban region (CURE), comprising Hyderabad, Rangareddy, Medchal Malkajgiri and Sangareddy districts, would be resolved within 45 days. He had also announced that the relevant GOs and revised lists would be made available on the registration department’s IGRS (inspector general of registration and stamps) portal.However, applicants allege that progress has been uneven, with several cases continuing to remain pending, particularly in Sangareddy.Among them are N Sunil Kumar and N Rahul, who applied six months ago for removal of six acres of land in Kothur Pattikohir village of Kohir mandal from the prohibited list after it was classified as waqf land.“Though, there is high court order and mandal tehsildar report recommending removal from 22A, the application is still showing pending. The district authorities are asking us to approach Waqf Board, but the board officials said it is the district collector, who has to implement the high court order and remove from the list and Bhu Bharati,” Sunil Kumar, who is an applicant, told TOI.While registrations resumed in areas such as Jubilee Hills Cooperative House Building Society and other localities affected by urban land ceiling (ULC) disputes soon after the govt’s intervention, the revised prohibited property lists for Hyderabad district mandals are yet to be uploaded on the IGRS website, reportedly because they remain under review.The absence of updated lists has created uncertainty for buyers and sellers, who are unable to verify whether specific survey numbers fall under prohibited categories such as govt land, waqf properties, endowment lands or other restricted classifications. At present, only court case details and existing prohibited property records are available on the portal.Sources said that despite chief minister A Revanth Reddy and Srinivas Reddy stating that the govt had identified 12 categories of issues linked to prohibited properties, many district collectors have focused only on clearing pending applications rather than comprehensively revising and updating the lists.The govt has, however, taken several steps to address long-pending land disputes. These include orders relating to ULC regularisation, resolution of land regularisation issues in LB Nagar, and disposal of pending GO 59 applications concerning structures built on encroached govt land.Land laws expert M Sunil Kumar said a permanent solution would require greater transparency at the grassroots level. He suggested that the govt publish prohibited property lists in gram panchayats and invite objections and suggestions before finalising them.“In many districts, the collectors have uploaded the old lists which were there in earlier Dharani on Bhu Bharati portal. If there are any genuine issues, those can be resolved at the village level.
